title: FocalFormer3D : Focusing on Hard Instance for 3D Object Detection
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)

statements: FocalFormer3D : Focusing on Hard Instance for 3D Object Detection Abstract 3D object detection is an important yet challenging perception task.
In this work, we propose Hard Instance Probing (HIP), a general pipeline that identifies FN in a multi-stage manner and guides the models to focus on excavating difficult instances.
For 3D object detection, we instantiate this method as FocalFormer3D, a simple yet effective detector that excels at excavating difficult objects and improving prediction recall.
Despite the tremendous efforts, there has been limited exploration to explicitly address false negatives or missed objects often caused by occlusions and clutter background.

deploymentClaims: Introduction True Positives Stage=2 False negatives (FN) in 3D object detection, e.g., missing predictions of pedestrians, vehicles, or other obstacles, can lead to potentially dangerous situations in autonomous driving.
False negatives are particularly concerning in autonomous driving as they cause missing information in the prediction and planning stacks.
Therefore, reducing false negatives is crucial to ensure the safety of autonomous driving.
